verdict: Apple's June quarter set records as iPhone sales jumped 22% and Services kept climbing — revenue rose 16% to $109.4B and profit hit $29.8B, even as iPad sales slipped.

segments.name: iPhone
segments.note: iPhone sales — about half of everything Apple sells; up 22% YoY to a June-quarter record.

segments.name: iPad
segments.note: iPad tablets; down 6% YoY against a strong launch quarter a year ago.

segments.name: Wearables, Home and Accessories
segments.note: Apple Watch, AirPods, HomePod and add-ons; up 6% YoY.

segments.name: Services
segments.note: App Store, iCloud, Apple Music, TV+, Pay and warranties — high-margin subscriptions and fees; up 12% to a record.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Spending to design future products and technologies; up 32% YoY.

opex.name: SG&A
opex.note: Sales, marketing and day-to-day running costs.

otherDetail: Other income of $572M, net — interest and investment results outside the product business.

takeaways.title: The iPhone had a record June quarter
takeaways.text: iPhone revenue rose 22% to $54.3B — half of Apple's total sales — and Mac jumped 29%. Only iPad fell, down 6% against last year's launch-boosted quarter.

takeaways.title: Services set another record
takeaways.text: Services revenue hit $30.7B, up 12%. Services cost only $7.5B to deliver, so this segment quietly supplies an outsized share of Apple's profit.

takeaways.title: Half of every sales dollar survives direct costs
takeaways.text: Gross margin was $54.8B on $109.4B of sales — a 50.1% gross margin — and Apple kept $29.8B as net profit, 27 cents of every revenue dollar.
